input.question: Which country benefited the most from the creation of the railways?
input.ground_truth: I think a good case can be made for Canada, which in its modern form was essentially *created* by the Canadian Pacific Railway. The vast land area of Russia was similarly bound together by the Trans-Siberian Railway. Even the American West, though it had cultural and political ties to the eastern states, wasn't economically integrated into the nation until the transcontinental railway routes were completed.

Okay! Imagine you have a big toy train set, and you live in a house far away from your friend’s house. Before the train, you had to walk a *really* long way to visit your friend. But then, someone builds a train track (the railway) between your house and your friend’s house. Now, you can get there super fast and bring lots of toys with you!

Now, think of countries as big houses, and the railway as a super-fast road for trains. When railways were built a long time ago, some countries could move things (like food, toys, and clothes) much faster and easier than before.

The country that benefited the most was **the United States**. Before the railways, it was really hard to move things from one side of the country to the other. But after the trains came, people and stuff could go from one place to another very quickly. This helped the country grow and become stronger and richer, because people could buy and sell things from far away much more easily.

So, the United States was like the kid who got a super cool train set and could visit friends and bring lots of toys much faster!
